prompt: Which of the following best describes the money market?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: A market in which the demand for money and the supply of money determine the equilibrium nominal interest rate

options.label: C
options.text: A market in which the demand for money alone determines the nominal interest rate regardless of money supply

options.label: D
options.text: A market in which the supply of money alone determines how much money people choose to hold at every interest rate

options.label: E
options.text: A market in which the quantity of money demanded and supplied are measured against the price level rather than an interest rate

explanation: The money market brings money demand and money supply together to determine the equilibrium nominal interest rate. Equilibrium occurs where the quantities of money demanded and supplied are equal.

prompt: The money demand curve slopes downward because the quantity of money demanded

options.label: A

options.label: B

prompt: If the nominal interest rate increases, which of the following will most likely occur along a given money demand curve?

options.label: A
options.text: The quantity of money demanded will increase.

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity of money demanded will remain unchanged.

options.label: C
options.text: The quantity of money demanded will decrease.

options.label: D
options.text: The quantity of money supplied will decrease along the money supply curve.

options.label: E
options.text: The quantity of money supplied will increase while money demand remains unchanged.

explanation: A higher nominal interest rate corresponds to a lower quantity of money demanded on the downward-sloping money demand curve. This is a movement along the existing money demand curve.

prompt: If the nominal interest rate decreases, which of the following will most likely occur along a given money demand curve?

options.label: A
options.text: The quantity of money demanded will decrease.

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity of money demanded will increase.

options.text: The quantity of money demanded will remain unchanged.

options.label: D
options.text: The quantity of money supplied will decrease with the interest rate.

options.label: E
options.text: The money supply curve will become downward sloping.

explanation: A lower nominal interest rate corresponds to a larger quantity of money demanded. The change is represented by movement down and to the right along the money demand curve.

options.text: It is vertical because the quantity of money supplied is independent of the nominal interest rate.

options.label: A
